sentences.zh: 沁源河東郡河東郡後魏曰秦州，後周改曰蒲州。

translations.literal: Tongdi. Hedong Commandery: Hedong Commandery—Later Wei called it Qinzhou; Later Zhou changed it to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongdi. Hedong Commandery. Hedong Commandery. Later Wei called it Qinzhou; Later Zhou changed it to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣十，戶十五萬七千七十八。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 10 counties with a registered population of 157,078 households.

sentences.zh: 河東舊曰蒲阪縣，置河東郡。開皇初郡廢，十六年析置河東縣。大業初置河東郡，並蒲阪入。有酒官。有首山。有媯、汭水。桑泉開皇十六年置。有三疑山。汾陰舊置汾陰郡，開皇初郡廢。有龍門山。龍門後魏置，並置龍門郡。開皇初郡廢。芮城舊置，曰安戎。後周改焉，又置永樂郡，後省入焉。有關官。安邑開皇十六年置虞州，大業初州廢。有鹽池、銀冶。夏舊置安邑郡，開皇初郡廢。有巫鹹山、稷山、虞阪。河北舊置河北郡，開皇初郡廢。有關官。有砥柱山。有傅岩。猗氏西魏改曰桑泉，後周複焉。虞鄉後魏曰安定，西魏改曰南解，又改曰綏化，又曰虞鄉。有石錐山、百梯山、百徑山。絳郡後魏置東雍州，後周改曰絳州。

translations.literal: Hedong was formerly called Puban County, where Hedong Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year sixteen Hedong County was divided off and established. At the beginning of Daye, Hedong Commandery was established and Puban was merged into it. It had wine offices. It had Shou Mountain and the Gui and Rui rivers. Sangquan was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Sanyi Mountain. Fenyin formerly had Fenyin Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Longmen Mountain. Longmen was established by Later Wei, and Longmen Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Ruicheng was formerly established and called Anrong. Later Zhou changed it, and also established Yongle Commandery, later abolishing it into Ruicheng. It had barrier offices. Anyi had Yuzhou established in Kaihuang year sixteen; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had salt ponds and silver smelteries. Xia formerly had Anyi Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Wuxian Mountain, Ji Mountain, and Yu Slope. Hebei formerly had Hebei Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had barrier offices. It had Dizhu Mountain and Fu Cliff. Yishi was changed by Western Wei to Sangquan, and Later Zhou restored the old name. Yuxiang was called Anding by Later Wei; Western Wei changed it to Nanjie, then changed it to Suihua, and again called it Yuxiang. It had Shizhui Mountain, Baiti Mountain, and Baijing Mountain. Jiang Commandery had Eastern Yongzhou established by Later Wei; Later Zhou changed it to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶七萬一千八百七十六。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 8 counties with a registered population of 71,876 households.

sentences.zh: 正平舊曰臨汾，置正平郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。大業初置絳郡。又有後魏南絳郡，後周廢郡，又並南絳縣入小鄉縣。開皇十八年改曰汾東，大業初省入焉。翼城後魏置，曰北絳縣，並置北絳郡。後齊廢新安縣，並南絳郡入焉。開皇初郡廢，十八年改為翼城。有烏嶺山、東涇山。有澮水。絳舊置絳郡，開皇初郡廢。後周置晉州，建德五年廢。曲沃後周置，建德六年廢。有絳山、橋山。稷山后魏曰高涼，開皇十八年改焉。有後魏龍門郡，開皇初廢。又有後周勳州，置總管，後改曰絳州，開皇初移。聞喜有景山。有董澤陂。垣後魏置邵郡及白水縣。後周置邵州，改白水為亳城。開皇初郡廢。大業初州廢，縣改為垣縣，又省後魏所置清廉縣及後周所置蒲原縣入焉。有黑山。太平後魏置，後齊省臨汾縣入焉。有關官。文城郡東魏置南汾州，後周改為汾州，後齊為西汾州。

translations.literal: Zhengping was formerly called Linfen, where Zhengping Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye, Jiang Commandery was established. It also had Southern Jiang Commandery of Later Wei; Later Zhou abolished the commandery and also merged Southern Jiang County into Xiaoxiang County. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Fendong, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Zhengping. Yicheng was established by Later Wei and called Northern Jiang County, and Northern Jiang Commandery was also established. Later Qi abolished Xin'an County and merged Southern Jiang Commandery into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen it was changed to Yicheng. It had Wuling Mountain and Dongjing Mountain. It had the Hui River. Jiang formerly had Jiang Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Later Zhou established Jinzhou, which was abolished in Jiande year five. Quwo was established by Later Zhou and abolished in Jiande year six. It had Jiang Mountain and Qiao Mountain. Jishan was called Gaoliang by Later Wei; in Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed. It had Later Wei's Longmen Commandery, abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. It also had Xunzhou of Later Zhou, where an area commandant was established; later it was changed to Jiangzhou, and at the beginning of Kaihuang it was moved. Wenxi had Jing Mountain and Dongze Marsh. Yuan had Shao Commandery and Baishui County established by Later Wei. Later Zhou established Shaozhou and changed Baishui to Bocheng. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, the county was changed to Yuan County, and Qinglian County established by Later Wei and Puyuan County established by Later Zhou were also abolished into it. It had Hei Mountain. Taiping was established by Later Wei, and Later Qi abolished Linfen County into it. It had barrier offices. Wencheng Commandery had Southern Fenzhou established by Eastern Wei; Later Zhou changed it to Fenzhou, and Later Qi made it Western Fenzhou.

translations.idiomatic: When Later Zhou pacified Qi, a grand administrative office was established, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年府廢，十六年改為耿州，後複為汾州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, the office was abolished; in the sixteenth year it was changed to Gengzhou, afterward again restored as Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, the office was abolished; in the sixteenth year it was changed to Gengzhou, afterward again restored as Fenzhou, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 統縣四，戶二萬二千三百。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 4 counties with a registered population of 22,300 households.

sentences.zh: 吉昌後魏曰定陽縣，並置定陽郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。大業初，置文城郡。有風山。文城後魏置。有石門山。伍城後魏置，曰刑軍縣，後改為伍城，後又置伍城郡。開皇初郡廢，又廢後魏平昌縣入焉。大業初又廢大寧縣入焉。昌甯後魏置，並內陽郡。開皇初郡廢。有壺口山，崿山。臨汾郡後魏置唐州，改曰晉州。

At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye, Wencheng Commandery was established. It had Feng Mountain. Wencheng was established by Later Wei. It had Shimen Mountain. Wucheng was established by Later Wei and called Xingjun County; later it was changed to Wucheng, and later still Wucheng Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and Pingchang County of Later Wei was also abolished into it. At the beginning of Daye, Daning County was also abolished into it. sentences.zh: 後周置總管府，開皇初府廢。

translations.literal: Later Zhou established a grand administrative office; at the beginning of Kaihuang the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou established a grand administrative office; at the beginning of Kaihuang the office was abolished, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 臨汾後魏曰平陽，並置平陽郡。開皇初改郡為平河，改縣為臨汾，尋郡廢。又有東魏西河、敷城、伍城、北伍城、定陽等五郡，後周廢為西河、定陽二郡。開皇初郡並廢。又有後魏永安縣，開皇初改為西河，大業初省。又有舊襄城縣，後齊省。有姑射山。襄陵後魏太武禽赫連昌，乃分置禽昌縣。齊並襄陵入禽昌縣。大業初又改為襄陵。冀氏後魏置冀氏郡，領冀氏、合陽二縣。後齊郡廢，又廢合陽入焉。楊霍邑後魏曰永安，並置永安郡。開皇初郡廢。十六年置汾州，十八年改為呂州，縣曰霍邑。大業初州廢。有霍山。有彘水。汾西後魏曰臨汾，並置汾西郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改為汾西。又有後周新城縣，開皇十年省入。岳陽後魏置，曰安澤。大業初改焉。龍泉郡後周置汾州。

translations.literal: Linfen was called Pingyang by Later Wei, and Pingyang Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was changed to Pinghe and the county to Linfen, and soon the commandery was abolished. It also had five commanderies of Eastern Wei: Xihe, Fucheng, Wucheng, Northern Wucheng, and Dingyang. Later Zhou abolished them and made Xihe and Dingyang commanderies. At the beginning of Kaihuang both commanderies were abolished. It also had Yong'an County of Later Wei, changed to Xihe at the beginning of Kaihuang and abolished at the beginning of Daye. It also had old Xiangcheng County, abolished by Later Qi. It had Gushe Mountain. Xiangling: after Emperor Taiwu of Later Wei captured Helian Chang, Qinchang County was divided off and established. Qi merged Xiangling into Qinchang County. At the beginning of Daye it was again changed to Xiangling. Jishi had Jishi Commandery established by Later Wei, governing Jishi and Heyang counties. Later Qi abolished the commandery and also abolished Heyang into it. Yang and Huoyi: Huoyi was called Yong'an by Later Wei, and Yong'an Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Fenzhou was established; in year eighteen it was changed to Lüzhou, and the county was called Huoyi. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. It had Huo Mountain and the Zhi River. Fenxi was called Linfen by Later Wei, and Fenxi Commandery was also established there. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year eighteen the county was changed to Fenxi. It also had Xincheng County of Later Zhou, which in Kaihuang year ten was abolished into it. Yueyang was established by Later Wei and called Anze. At the beginning of Daye it was changed. Longquan Commandery had Fenzhou established by Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 隰川後周置縣，初曰長壽，又置龍泉郡。開皇初郡廢，縣改曰隰川。大業初置郡。永和後周置，曰臨河縣及臨河郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。有關官。樓山後周置，曰歸化。開皇十八年改名焉。有北石樓山，有孔山。石樓舊置吐京郡及吐京縣，開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名。蒲後周置，有伍城郡及石城郡及石城縣，週末並廢。又有後魏平昌縣，開皇中改曰蒲川，大業初廢入焉。西河郡後魏置汾州，後齊置南朔州，後周改曰介州。

translations.literal: Xichuan had a county established by Later Zhou, first called Changshou, and Longquan Commandery was also established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was changed to Xichuan. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was established. Yonghe was established by Later Zhou as Linhe County and Linhe Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. It had barrier offices. Loushan was established by Later Zhou and called Guihua; in Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. It had Northern Shilou Mountain and Kong Mountain. Shilou formerly had Tujing Commandery and Tujing County established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. Pu was established by Later Zhou; it had Wucheng Commandery, Shicheng Commandery, and Shicheng County, all abolished at the end of Zhou. It also had Pingchang County of Later Wei, changed during Kaihuang to Puchuan and abolished into Pu at the beginning of Daye. Xihe Commandery had Fenzhou established by Later Wei; Later Qi established Southern Shuozhou; Later Zhou changed it to Jiezhou.

translations.literal: Xicheng formerly had Xihe Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. It had Yinquan Mountain. Jiexiu had Dingyang Commandery and Pingchang County established by Later Wei. Later Zhou changed the commandery to Jiexiu and merged Jiexiu County into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county was changed to Jiexiu. Yong'an had Queshu Valley. sentences.zh: 雁門舊曰廣武，置雁門郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年改曰雁門。大業初置雁門郡。有關官。有長城。有摐頭山，有夏屋山。繁畤後魏置，並置繁畤郡。後周郡縣並廢。開皇十八年復置縣。有東魏武州及吐京、齊、新安三郡，寄在城中。後齊改為北靈州，尋廢。有長城、滹沱水、泒水、唐山。崞後魏置，曰石城縣。東魏置廓州。有廣安、永定、建安三郡，寄山城。後齊廢郡。改為北顯州。後周廢。開皇十年改縣曰平寇。大業初改為崞縣。又有雲中城，東魏僑置恆州，尋廢。有無京山、崞山。有土城。五台舊曰慮虒，久廢。後魏置，曰驢夷。大業初改焉。有五臺山。靈丘後魏置靈丘郡，後齊省莎泉縣入焉。後周置蔚州，又立大昌縣。開皇初郡廢，縣併入焉。大業初州廢。馬邑郡舊置朔州。

translations.literal: Yanmen was formerly called Guangwu, where Yanmen Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen it was changed to Yanmen. At the beginning of Daye, Yanmen Commandery was established. It had barrier offices and the Great Wall. It had Congtou Mountain and Xiawu Mountain. Fanshi was established by Later Wei, and Fanshi Commandery was also established. Later Zhou abolished both commandery and county. In Kaihuang year eighteen the county was restored. It had Eastern Wei's Wuzhou and Tujing, Qi, and Xin'an commanderies, lodged in the city. Later Qi changed it to Northern Lingzhou, soon abolished. It had the Great Wall, the Hutuo River, the Gu River, and Tang Mountain. Guo was established by Later Wei and called Shicheng County. Eastern Wei established Kuozhou. Guang'an, Yongding, and Jian'an commanderies were lodged at the mountain city. Later Qi abolished the commanderies and changed it to Northern Xianzhou. Later Zhou abolished it. In Kaihuang year ten the county was changed to Pingkou. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Guo County. It also had Yunzhong City, where Eastern Wei established Hengzhou in exile, soon abolished. It had Wujing Mountain and Guo Mountain. It had Tucheng. Wutai was formerly called Luyi and had long been abolished. Later Wei established it and called it Luyi. At the beginning of Daye it was changed. It had Wutai Mountain. Lingqiu had Lingqiu Commandery established by Later Wei; Later Qi abolished Shaquan County into it. Later Zhou established Weizhou and also set up Dachang County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and the county was merged into Lingqiu. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Mayi Commandery formerly had Shuozhou established.

translations.literal: Shanyang was established by Later Qi; the county was called Zhaoyuan and the commandery Guang'an. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. At the beginning of Daye the county was changed to Shanyang, Dai Commandery was established, and soon it was called Mayi. It also had Sanggan Commandery of Later Wei; Later Qi used it to establish Shuozhou and Guangning Commandery. Later Zhou abolished the commandery, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Shenwu had Shenwu Commandery established by Later Wei; Later Qi changed it to Taiping, and Later Zhou abolished the commandery. It had the Sanggan River. Yunnei had Pingqi Commandery established by Later Wei, soon abolished. Later Qi changed it to Taiping County; Later Zhou changed it to Yunzhong; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was changed to Yunnei. It had the capital of Later Wei, where Sizhou was established, and also had Anyuan, Linsai, Weiyuan, and Linyang commanderies of Later Qi belonging to Northern Hengzhou; Later Zhou abolished all of them. It had Chunzhen Mountain, Baideng Mountain, and Wuzhou Mountain. It had the Shi River. Kaiyang was formerly called Changning. Later Qi established Qide and Changning commanderies. Later Zhou abolished Qide Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year nineteen the county was changed to Kaiyang. Dingxiang Commandery had the Yunzhou area commandant's office established in Kaihuang year five; in Daye year one the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大利大業初置，帶郡。有長城。有陰山。有紫河。樓煩郡大業四年置。

translations.literal: Dali was established at the beginning of Daye and carried the commandery. It had the Great Wall, Yin Mountain, and the Zi River. Loufan Commandery was established in Daye year four.
translations.idiomatic: Dali was established at the beginning of Daye and carried the commandery. It had the Great Wall, Yin Mountain, and the Zi River. Loufan Commandery was established in Daye year four.

sentences.zh: 統縣三，戶二萬四千四百二十七。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 3 counties with a registered population of 24,427 households.

sentences.zh: 靜樂舊曰岢嵐。開皇十八年改為汾源，大業四年改焉。有長城。有汾陽宮。有關官。有管涔山、天池、汾水。臨泉後齊置，曰蔚汾。大業四年改焉。秀容舊置肆州，後齊又置平寇縣。後周州徙雁門。開皇初置新興郡、銅川縣。郡尋廢。十年廢平寇縣。十八年置忻州，大業初州廢，又廢銅川。有程侯山、系舟山。有嵐水。太原郡後齊并州，置省，立別宮。

translations.literal: Jingle was formerly called Kelan. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Fenyuan, and in Daye year four it was changed again. It had the Great Wall, Fenyang Palace, and barrier offices. It had Guancen Mountain, Heaven Pool, and the Fen River. Linquan was established by Later Qi and called Weifen. In Daye year four it was changed. Xiurong formerly had Sizhou established; Later Qi also established Pingkou County. Later Zhou moved the province to Yanmen. At the beginning of Kaihuang, Xinxing Commandery and Tongchuan County were established. The commandery was soon abolished. In year ten Pingkou County was abolished. In year eighteen Xinzhou was established; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Tongchuan was also abolished. It had Chenghou Mountain and Xizhou Mountain. It had the Lan River. Taiyuan Commandery: Later Qi had Bingzhou there, established a bureau, and set up a detached palace.

translations.literal: Xiurong. Taiyuan Commandery: Taiyuan Commandery—Northern Qi made it Bingzhou, established a provincial office, and built a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 後周置并州六府，後置總管，廢六府。

translations.literal: Later Zhou established the six offices of Bingzhou, afterward established a grand administrator and abolished the six offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou established the six offices of Bingzhou, afterward established a grand administrator and abolished the six offices, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年置河北道行台，九年改為總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, the Hebei Circuit field headquarters was established; in the ninth year it was changed to a grand administrative office; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang, the Hebei Circuit field headquarters was established; in the ninth year it was changed to a grand administrative office; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 統縣十五，戶十七萬五千三。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 15 counties with a registered population of 175,003 households.

sentences.zh: 晉陽後齊置，曰龍山。帶太原郡。開皇初郡廢，十年改縣曰晉陽，十六年又置清源縣，大業初省入焉。有龍山、蒙山。太原舊曰晉陽，帶郡。開皇十年分置陽真縣，大業初省入焉。有晉陽宮。有晉水。交城開皇十六年置。汾陽舊曰陽曲。開皇六年改為陽直，十六年又改名焉，復分置孟縣，大業初廢。有摩笄山。文水舊曰受陽，開皇十年改焉。有文水、泌水。祁後齊廢，開皇中復。壽陽開皇十年改州南受陽縣為文水，分州東故壽陽置壽陽。有甗岩。榆次後齊曰中都，開皇中改焉。太谷舊曰陽邑，開皇十八年改焉。樂平舊置樂平郡，開皇初廢郡。十六年分置遼州及東山縣，大業初廢州及東山縣。有皋洛山。有清漳水。和順舊曰梁榆，開皇十年改。有九京山。遼山後魏曰遼陽，後齊省。開皇十年置，改名焉。十六年屬遼州，並置交漳縣。大業初廢州，並罷交漳入焉。有萁轑水。平城開皇十六年置。有塗水。石艾有蒙山。孟開皇十六年置，曰原仇，大業初改焉。有白鹿山。襄國郡開皇十六年置邢州。

translations.literal: Jinyang was established by Later Qi and called Longshan. It carried Taiyuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year ten the county was changed to Jinyang, and in year sixteen Qingyuan County was also established; at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Jinyang. It had Long Mountain and Meng Mountain. Taiyuan was formerly called Jinyang and carried a commandery. In Kaihuang year ten Yangzhen County was divided off and established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Taiyuan. It had Jinyang Palace and the Jin River. Jiaocheng was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. Fenyang was formerly called Yangqu. In Kaihuang year six it was changed to Yangzhi, and in year sixteen its name was changed again; Meng County was again divided off and established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished. It had Moji Mountain. Wenshui was formerly called Shouyang; in Kaihuang year ten it was changed. It had the Wenshui and Bi rivers. Qi was abolished by Later Qi and restored during Kaihuang. Shouyang: in Kaihuang year ten, Shouyang County south of the province was changed to Wenshui, and old Shouyang east of the province was divided off to establish Shouyang. It had Yan Cliff. Yuci was called Zhongdu by Later Qi, and during Kaihuang it was changed. Taigu was formerly called Yangyi; in Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed. Leping formerly had Leping Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Liaozhou and Dongshan County were divided off and established; at the beginning of Daye the province and Dongshan County were abolished. It had Gaoluo Mountain and the Qingzhang River. Heshun was formerly called Liangyu; in Kaihuang year ten it was changed. It had Jiujing Mountain. Liaoshan was called Liaoyang by Later Wei and was abolished by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year ten it was established and its name was changed. In year sixteen it belonged to Liaozhou, and Jiaozhang County was also established. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and Jiaozhang was also discontinued and merged into it. It had the Qiliao River. Pingcheng was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had the Tu River. Shi'ai had Meng Mountain. Meng was established in Kaihuang year sixteen and called Yuanqiu; at the beginning of Daye it was changed. It had Bailu Mountain. Xiangguo Commandery had Xingzhou established in Kaihuang year sixteen.

sentences.zh: 孟襄國郡襄國郡開皇十六年置邢州。

translations.literal: Meng. Xiangguo Commandery: Xiangguo Commandery—in the sixteenth year of Kaihuang, Xingzhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Meng. Xiangguo Commandery. Xiangguo Commandery. in the sixteenth year of Kaihuang, Xingzhou was established.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戶十萬五千八百七十三。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 7 counties with a registered population of 105,873 households.

sentences.zh: 龍岡舊曰襄國，開皇九年改名焉。十六年又置青山縣，大業初省入焉。有黑山。有干水。南和舊置北廣平郡，後齊省入廣平郡，後周分置南和郡。開皇初郡廢，十六年置任縣，大業初廢入。平鄉沙河開皇十六置。有罄山。钜鹿後齊廢，開皇六年置南䜌縣，後廢入焉。內丘有干言山。柏仁有鵲山。武安郡後周置洛州。

translations.literal: Longgang was formerly called Xiangguo; in Kaihuang year nine its name was changed. In year sixteen Qingshan County was also established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Longgang. It had Hei Mountain and the Gan River. Nanhe formerly had Northern Guangping Commandery established; Later Qi abolished it into Guangping Commandery, and Later Zhou divided off and established Nanhe Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished; in year sixteen Ren County was established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Nanhe. Pingxiang and Shahe: Shahe was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Qing Mountain. Julu was abolished by Later Qi; in Kaihuang year six Nanluan County was established, and later it was abolished into Julu. Neiqiu had Ganyan Mountain. Bairen had Que Mountain. Wu'an Commandery had Luozhou established by Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 柏仁武安郡武安郡後周置洛州。

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶十一萬八千五百九十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 8 counties with a registered population of 118,595 households.

sentences.zh: 永年舊曰廣平，置廣平郡，後齊廢北廣平郡及曲梁、廣平二縣入。開皇初郡廢，復置廣平，後改曰雞澤。仁壽元年改廣平為永年。大業初置武安郡，又並雞澤縣入。肥鄉東魏省，開皇十年復。清漳開皇十六年置。平恩洺水舊曰斥漳，後齊省入平恩。開皇六年分置曲周，大業初廢入焉。武安開皇十年分置陽邑縣，大業初廢入焉。有榆溪，有閼與山，有浸水。邯鄲東魏廢。開皇十六年復置陟鄉，大業初省入焉。臨洺舊曰易陽。後齊廢入襄國縣，置襄國郡。後周改為易陽縣，別置襄國縣。開皇六年改易陽為邯鄲，十年改邯鄲為臨洺。開皇初郡廢。有紫山、狗山、塔山。趙郡開皇十六年置欒州，大業三年改為趙州。

translations.literal: Yongnian was formerly called Guangping, where Guangping Commandery was established; Later Qi abolished Northern Guangping Commandery and Quliang and Guangping counties into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished and Guangping was restored; later it was changed to Jize. In Renshou year one Guangping was changed to Yongnian. At the beginning of Daye, Wu'an Commandery was established, and Jize County was also merged into it. Feixiang was abolished by Eastern Wei and restored in Kaihuang year ten. Qingzhang was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. Ping'en and Mingshui: Mingshui was formerly called Chizhang, and Later Qi abolished it into Ping'en. In Kaihuang year six Quzhou was divided off and established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Ping'en. Wu'an had Yangyi County divided off and established in Kaihuang year ten; at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Wu'an. It had Yu Creek, Eyu Mountain, and Qin River. Handan was abolished by Eastern Wei. In Kaihuang year sixteen Zhixiang was restored, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Handan. Linming was formerly called Yiyang. Later Qi abolished it into Xiangguo County and established Xiangguo Commandery. Later Zhou changed it to Yiyang County and separately established Xiangguo County. In Kaihuang year six Yiyang was changed to Handan; in year ten Handan was changed to Linming. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had Zi Mountain, Gou Mountain, and Ta Mountain. Zhao Commandery had Luanzhou established in Kaihuang year sixteen; in Daye year three it was changed to Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣十一，戶十四萬八千一百五十六。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 11 counties with a registered population of 148,156 households.

sentences.zh: 平棘舊置趙郡，開皇初省。有宋子縣，後齊廢。大業初置趙郡，廢宋子縣入焉。高邑贊皇開皇十六年置。有孔子嶺，有白溝。元氏舊縣，後齊廢，開皇六年置。大業初置趙郡，廢宋子縣入焉。癭陶舊曰癭遙，開皇六年改為「陶」。欒城舊縣，後齊廢，開皇十六年復。大陸舊曰廣阿，置殷州及南鉅鹿郡。後改為南趙郡，改州為趙州。開皇十六年分置欒州，仁壽元年改為象城。大業初州廢，縣改為大陸。又開皇十六年所置大陸縣，亦廢入焉。栢鄉開皇十六年置。有𡺟𡺱山。房子舊縣，後齊省，開皇六年復。有贊皇山。有彭水。稾城後齊廢下曲陽入焉。改為高城縣，置鉅鹿郡。開皇初郡廢。十年置廉州，十八年改為稾城縣，大業初州廢。又開皇十六年置栢鄉縣，亦廢入焉。鼓城舊曰曲陽，後齊廢。開皇十六年分置昔陽縣，十八年改為鼓城。十六年又置廉平縣，大業初併入。恆山郡後周置恆州。

translations.literal: Pingji formerly had Zhao Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was abolished. It had Songzi County, abolished by Later Qi. At the beginning of Daye, Zhao Commandery was established, and Songzi County was abolished into it. Gaoyi and Zanhuang: Zanhuang was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Kongzi Ridge and Bai Ditch. Yuanshi was an old county, abolished by Later Qi and established in Kaihuang year six. At the beginning of Daye, Zhao Commandery was established, and Songzi County was abolished into it. Yingtao was formerly called Yingyao; in Kaihuang year six it was changed to "Tao". Luancheng was an old county, abolished by Later Qi and restored in Kaihuang year sixteen. Dalu was formerly called Guang'e, where Yinzhou and Southern Julu Commandery were established. Later it was changed to Southern Zhao Commandery, and the province was changed to Zhaozhou. In Kaihuang year sixteen Luanzhou was divided off and established; in Renshou year one it was changed to Xiangcheng. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and the county was changed to Dalu. Dalu County, established in Kaihuang year sixteen, was also abolished into it. Baixiang was established in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Miao'ao Mountain. Fangzi was an old county, abolished by Later Qi and restored in Kaihuang year six. It had Zanhuang Mountain and the Peng River. Gaocheng had Xiaquyang abolished into it by Later Qi. It was changed to Gaocheng County, and Julu Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year ten Lianzhou was established; in year eighteen it was changed to Gaocheng County, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Baixiang County, established in Kaihuang year sixteen, was also abolished into it. Gucheng was formerly called Quyang and was abolished by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year sixteen Xiyang County was divided off and established; in year eighteen it was changed to Gucheng. In year sixteen Lianping County was also established, and at the beginning of Daye it was merged into Gucheng. Hengshan Commandery had Hengzhou established by Later Zhou.

translations.literal: Gucheng. Hengshan Commandery: Hengshan Commandery—Later Zhou established Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng. Hengshan Commandery. Hengshan Commandery. Later Zhou established Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣八，戶十七萬七千五百七十一。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 8 counties with a registered population of 177,571 households.

sentences.zh: 真定舊置常山郡，開皇初郡廢。十六年分置常山縣。大業初置恆山郡，省常山入焉。滋陽開皇六年置。十六年又置玉亭縣，大業初省入焉。有大茂山、歲山。行唐石邑舊縣，後齊改曰井陘，開皇六年改焉。十六年析置鹿泉縣，大業初併入。有封龍山、抱犢山。九門後齊廢，開皇六年復。大業初，又並新市縣入焉。有許春壘。井陘後齊廢石邑，以置井陘。開皇六年復石邑縣，分置井陘。十六年于井陘置井州，及置葦澤縣。大業初廢州，並廢葦澤縣及蒲吾縣入焉。房山開皇十六年置。靈壽後周置蒲吾郡，開皇初郡廢。博陵郡舊置定州。

translations.literal: Zhending formerly had Changshan Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Changshan County was divided off and established. At the beginning of Daye, Hengshan Commandery was established, and Changshan was abolished into it. Ziyang was established in Kaihuang year six. In year sixteen Yuting County was also established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Ziyang. It had Damao Mountain and Sui Mountain. Hengyang was formerly called Shangquyang; Later Qi removed the shang character. In Kaihuang year six it was changed to Shiyi, and in year seven it was changed to Hengyang. sentences.zh: 河間舊置河間郡，開皇初郡廢。大業初復置郡，並武垣縣入焉。文安有狐狸澱。樂壽舊曰樂城，開皇十八年改為廣城，仁壽初改焉。束城舊曰束州，後齊廢。開皇十六年置，後改名焉。景城舊曰成平，開皇十八年改焉。高陽舊置高陽郡，開皇初郡廢。十六年置蒲州，大業初州廢，並任丘縣入焉。鄚有易城縣，後齊廢。開皇中置永寧縣，大業初廢入焉。博野舊曰博陸，後魏改為博野，後齊廢蠡吾縣入焉。有君子澱。清苑舊曰樂鄉。後齊省樊興、北新城、清苑、樂鄉入永寧，改名焉。開皇十八年改為清苑。長蘆開皇初置，並立漳河郡，郡尋廢。十六年置景州，大業初州廢。平舒舊置章武郡，開皇初廢。魯城開皇十六年置。饒陽開皇十六年分置安平、蕪蔞二縣，大業初省入焉。涿郡舊置幽州，後齊置東北道行台。

Leshou was formerly called Lecheng; in Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Guangcheng, and at the beginning of Renshou it was changed. Shucheng was formerly called Shuzhou and was abolished by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year sixteen it was established, and later its name was changed. Jingcheng was formerly called Chengping; in Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed. Gaoyang formerly had Gaoyang Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Puzhou was established, and at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished and Renqiu County was merged into it. Mo had Yicheng County, abolished by Later Qi. During Kaihuang Yongning County was established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Mo. Boye was formerly called Bolu; Later Wei changed it to Boye, and Later Qi abolished Liwu County into it. It had Junzi Marsh. Qingyuan was formerly called Lexiang. In year six it was changed to Gu'an, in year eight abolished, in year ten established again as Yongyang, and in year eighteen changed to Laishui. sentences.zh: 燕樂後魏置廣陽郡，領大興、方城、燕樂三縣。後齊廢郡，以大興、方城入焉。大業初置安樂郡。有長城。有沽河。密雲後魏置密雲郡，領白檀、要陽、密雲三縣。後齊廢郡及二縣入密雲。又有舊安樂郡，領安市、土垠二縣，後齊廢土垠入安市，後周廢安市入密雲縣。開皇初郡廢。有長城。有桃花山、螺山。有漁水。遼西郡舊置營州，開皇初置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Yanle had Guangyang Commandery established by Later Wei, governing Daxing, Fangcheng, and Yanle counties. Later Qi abolished the commandery and merged Daxing and Fangcheng into Yanle. At the beginning of Daye, Anle Commandery was established. It had the Great Wall and the Gu River. Miyun had Miyun Commandery established by Later Wei, governing Baitan, Yaoyang, and Miyun counties. Later Qi abolished the commandery and two counties into Miyun. It also had old Anle Commandery, governing Anshi and Tuyin counties; Later Qi abolished Tuyin into Anshi, and Later Zhou abolished Anshi into Miyun County. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. It had the Great Wall. It had Taohua Mountain and Luo Mountain. It had the Yu River. Liaoxi Commandery formerly had Yingzhou established; at the beginning of Kaihuang an area commandant's office was established, and at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 密雲遼西郡遼西郡舊置營州，開皇初置總管府，大業初府廢。

translations.literal: Miyun. Liaoxi Commandery: Liaoxi Commandery formerly had Yingzhou established; at the beginning of Kaihuang a grand administrative office was established; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Miyun. Liaoxi Commandery, Liaoxi Commandery had formerly had Yingzhou established; at the beginning of Kaihuang a grand administrative office was established; at the beginning of Daye the office was abolished.

translations.literal: It governed one county with 751 households.
translations.idiomatic: It had jurisdiction over one county with 751 households.

sentences.zh: 柳城後魏置營州于和龍城，領建德、冀陽、昌黎、遼東、樂浪、營丘等郡，龍城、大興、永樂、帶方、定荒、石城、廣都、陽武、襄平、新昌、平剛、柳城、富平等縣。後齊唯留建德、冀陽二郡，永樂、帶方、龍城、大興等縣，其餘並廢。開皇元年唯留建德一郡，龍城一縣，其餘並廢。尋又廢郡，改縣為龍山，十八年改為柳城。大業初，置遼西郡。有帶方山、禿黎山、雞鳴山、松山。有渝水、白狼水。

translations.literal: Liu City: Later Wei established Yingzhou at Helong City, governing Jiande, Jiyang, Changli, Liaodong, Lelang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies, and Longcheng, Daxing, Yongle, Daifang, Dinghuang, Shicheng, Guangdu, Yangwu, Xiangping, Xinchang, Pinggang, Liucheng, Fuping, and other counties. Later Qi left only Jiande and Jiyang commanderies and Yongle, Daifang, Longcheng, Daxing, and other counties; the rest were all abolished. In Kaihuang year one, only Jiande Commandery and Longcheng County were left, and the rest were all abolished. Soon the commandery was also abolished, and the county was changed to Longshan; in year eighteen it was changed to Liucheng. At the beginning of Daye, Liaoxi Commandery was established. It had Daifang Mountain, Tuli Mountain, Jiming Mountain, and Song Mountain. It had the Yu River and Bailang River.

translations.literal: In antiquity, Ji Province was the capital region of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Ji Province was the capital region of Yao, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 舜分州為十二，冀州析置幽、并。

translations.literal: When Shun divided the provinces into twelve, Ji Province was subdivided to establish You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun divided the provinces into twelve, Ji Province was subdivided to establish You and Bing, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其于天文，自胃七度至畢十一度，為大樑，屬冀州。

translations.literal: In astronomy, from seven degrees of Wei to eleven degrees of Bi is the Great Bridge asterism, belonging to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In astronomy, from seven degrees of Wei to eleven degrees of Bi is the Great Bridge asterism, belonging to Ji Province, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自尾十度至南斗十一度，為析木，屬幽州。

translations.literal: From ten degrees of Wei to eleven degrees of Nandou is the Suggesting Wood asterism, belonging to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: From ten degrees of Wei to eleven degrees of Nandou is the Suggesting Wood asterism, belonging to You Province, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自危十六度至奎四度，為娵訾，屬并州。

translations.literal: From sixteen degrees of Wei to four degrees of Kui is the JuZi asterism, belonging to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: From sixteen degrees of Wei to four degrees of Kui is the Ju Zi asterism, belonging to Bing Province, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 自柳九度至張十六度，為鶉火，屬三河，則河內、河東也。

translations.literal: From nine degrees of Liu to sixteen degrees of Zhang is the Quail Fire asterism, belonging to the Three Rivers—that is, Henei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: From nine degrees of Liu to sixteen degrees of Zhang is the Quail Fire asterism, belonging to the Three Rivers—that is, Henei and Hedong, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 准之星次，本皆冀州之域，帝居所在，故其界尤大。

translations.literal: The star stations of Huai were originally all within the domain of Ji Province; the imperial seat lay here, hence its bounds were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: The star stations of Huai were originally all within the domain of Ji Province; the imperial seat lay here, hence its bounds were especially great, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 至夏廢幽、併入焉，得唐之舊矣。

translations.literal: When Xia abolished You and Bing and merged them in, it recovered the old territory of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia abolished You and Bing and merged them in, it recovered the old territory of Tang, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 信都、清河、河間、博陵、恆山、趙郡、武安、襄國，其俗頗同。

translations.literal: Xindu, Qinghe, Hejian, Boling, Hengshan, Zhao, Wu'an, and Xiangguo commanderies share much the same customs.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu, Qinghe, Hejian, Boling, Hengshan, Zhao, Wu'an, and Xiangguo commanderies share much the same customs, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 人性多敦厚，務在農桑，好尚儒學，而傷于遲重。

translations.literal: The people's nature is largely sincere and generous; they devote themselves to farming and sericulture and esteem Confucian learning, yet they suffer from sluggish heaviness.
translations.idiomatic: The people's nature is largely sincere and generous; they devote themselves to farming and sericulture and esteem Confucian learning, yet they suffer from sluggish heaviness, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 前代稱冀、幽之士鈍如椎，蓋取此焉。

translations.literal: Former ages said the gentlemen of Ji and You were blunt as mallets—this is what was meant.
translations.idiomatic: Former ages said the gentlemen of Ji and You were blunt as mallets—this is what was meant, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 俗重氣俠，好結朋黨，其相赴死生，亦出於仁義。

translations.literal: The custom values spirited chivalry and loves forming cliques; their mutual devotion in life and death also springs from benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The custom values spirited chivalry and loves forming cliques; their mutual devotion in life and death also springs from benevolence and righteousness, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 故《班志》述其土風，悲歌慷慨，椎剽掘塚，亦自古之所患焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the Ban Treatise describes their local character: impassioned songs, generous laments, club robberies and grave robbing—these have been afflictions since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, the "Ban Treatise" describes their local character: impassioned songs, generous laments, club robberies and grave robbing—these have been afflictions since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 前諺雲「仕官不偶遇冀部」，實弊此也。

translations.literal: An old proverb says, "In taking office, do not happen to meet the Ji region"—the harm truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that "In taking office, do not happen to meet the Ji region"—the harm truly lies here.

sentences.zh: 魏郡，鄴都所在，浮巧成俗，雕刻之工，特雲精妙，士女被服，鹹以奢麗相高，其性所尚習，得京、洛之風矣。

translations.literal: Wei Commandery, where the capital of Ye stood, made floating cleverness the custom; the craft of carving was especially said to be exquisite and subtle; men and women in dress all vied in luxury and splendor—the inclinations they cultivated had acquired the air of the capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Commandery, where the capital of Ye stood, made floating cleverness the custom; the craft of carving was especially said to be exquisite and subtle; men and women in dress all vied in luxury and splendor—the inclinations they cultivated had acquired the air of the capitals, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「魏郡、清河，天公無奈何！」

translations.literal: People said: "Wei Commandery and Qinghe: Heaven can do nothing about them!"
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Wei Commandery and Qinghe: Heaven can do nothing about them!"

translations.literal: All these come from frivolity and cunning.
translations.idiomatic: All these come from frivolity and cunning, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 汲郡、河內，得殷之故壤，考之舊說，有紂之餘教。

translations.literal: Ji and Henei commanderies obtained the old soil of Yin; examining old accounts, remnants of Zhou's teaching remained.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Henei commanderies obtained the old soil of Yin; examining old accounts, remnants of Zhou's teaching remained, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 汲又衛地，習仲由之勇，故漢之官人，得以便宜從事，其多行殺戮，本以此焉。

translations.literal: Ji was also the land of Wei, accustomed to Zhong You's valor; hence Han officials could act at discretion, and their frequent resort to killing sprang from this.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was also the land of Wei, accustomed to Zhong You's valor; hence Han officials could act at discretion, and their frequent resort to killing sprang from this, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 今風俗頗移，皆向於禮矣。

translations.literal: Now the customs have shifted considerably, all turning toward ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By the present day, the customs have shifted considerably, all turning toward ritual.

sentences.zh: 長平、上黨，人多重農桑，性尤樸直，蓋少輕詐。

translations.literal: In Changping and Shangdang, people greatly value farming and sericulture; their nature is especially plain and straight, with little of light deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In Changping and Shangdang, people greatly value farming and sericulture; their nature is especially plain and straight, with little of light deceit, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 河東、絳郡、文城、臨汾、龍泉、西河，土地沃少瘠多，是以傷於儉嗇。

translations.literal: Hedong, Jiang, Wencheng, Linfen, Longquan, and Xihe—land fertile but with more barren than rich soil—hence they suffer from stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, Jiang, Wencheng, Linfen, Longquan, and Xihe—land fertile but with more barren than rich soil—hence they suffer from stinginess, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: Their customs are hard and strong—is this not also the effect of climate and air?
translations.idiomatic: Their customs are hard and strong—is this not also the effect of climate and air?

sentences.zh: 太原山川重複，實一都之會，本雖後齊別都，人物殷阜，然不甚機巧。

translations.literal: Taiyuan lies amid overlapping mountains and rivers and is truly the meeting place of a great capital; though originally the secondary capital of Later Qi, its population is abundant, yet it is not very artful.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan lies amid overlapping mountains and rivers and is truly the meeting place of a great capital; though originally the secondary capital of Later Qi, its population is abundant, yet it is not very artful, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 俗與上黨頗同，人性勁悍，習於戎馬。

translations.literal: Its customs resemble Shangdang considerably; the people's nature is fierce and bold, practiced in horses and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom resemble Shangdang considerably; the people's nature is fierce and bold, practiced in horses and arms.

sentences.zh: 離石、雁門、馬邑、定襄、樓煩、涿郡、上谷、漁陽、北平、安樂、遼西，皆連接邊郡，習尚與太原同俗，故自古言勇俠者，皆推幽、并雲。

translations.literal: Lishi, Yanmen, Mayi, Dingxiang, Loufan, Zhuo, Shanggu, Yuyang, Beiping, Anle, and Liaoxi—all connect with frontier commanderies and share customs much like Taiyuan; hence from antiquity those who speak of brave knights-errant all point to You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Lishi, Yanmen, Mayi, Dingxiang, Loufan, Zhuo, Shanggu, Yuyang, Beiping, Anle, and Liaoxi—all connect with frontier commanderies and share customs much like Taiyuan; hence from antiquity those who speak of brave knights-errant all point to You and Bing, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 然涿郡、太原，自前代已來，皆多文雅之士，雖俱曰邊郡，然風教不為比也。

translations.literal: Yet Zhuo and Taiyuan, from former ages onward, have produced many refined literary gentlemen; though both are called frontier commanderies, their culture and teaching are not to be compared alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhuo and Taiyuan, from former ages onward, have produced many refined literary gentlemen; though both are called frontier commanderies, their culture and teaching are not to be compared alike, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 青州北海郡北海郡舊置青州，後周置總管府，開皇十四年府廢。

translations.literal: Qing Province, Beihai Commandery: Beihai Commandery formerly had Qingzhou established; Later Zhou established a grand administrative office; in the fourteenth year of Kaihuang the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qing Province, Beihai Commandery, Beihai Commandery had formerly had Qingzhou established; Later Zhou established a grand administrative office; in the fourteenth year of Kaihuang the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 統縣十，戶十四萬七千八百四十五。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 10 counties with a registered population of 147,845 households.

sentences.zh: 益都舊置齊郡，開皇初廢，大業初置北海郡。有堯山、鋋山。臨淄及東安平、西安，並後齊廢。開皇十六年又置臨淄及時水縣。大業初廢高陽、時水二縣入焉。有社山、葵丘、牛山、稷山。千乘舊置樂安郡，開皇初郡廢。博昌舊曰樂安，開皇十六年改焉。又十八年析置新河縣，大業初廢入焉。壽光開皇十六年置閭丘縣，大業初廢入焉。臨朐舊曰昌國。開皇六年改為逢山，又置般陽縣。大業初改曰臨朐，並廢般陽入焉。有逢山、沂山、穆陵山、大峴山。有汶水、浯水。都昌有箕山、阜山、白狼山。北海舊曰下密，置北海郡。後齊改郡曰高陽，開皇初郡廢。十六年分置濰州，大業初州廢，縣改名焉。營丘後齊廢，開皇十六年複。有叢角山、女節山。下密後魏曰膠東，後齊廢。開皇六年複，改為濰水。大業初改名焉。有鐵山。有溉水。齊郡舊曰齊州。

translations.literal: Yidu formerly had Qi Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang it was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye Beihai Commandery was established. It had Yao Mountain and Chan Mountain. Linzi, Eastern Anping, and Xi'an were all abolished by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year sixteen Linzi and Shishui County were again established. At the beginning of Daye, Gaoyang and Shishui counties were abolished into Linzi. It had She Mountain, Kuiqiu, Niu Mountain, and Ji Mountain. Qiansheng formerly had Le'an Commandery established; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Bochang was formerly called Le'an; in Kaihuang year sixteen it was changed. In year eighteen Xinhe County was also divided off and established, and at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Bochang. Shouguang had Lüqiu County established in Kaihuang year sixteen; at the beginning of Daye it was abolished into Shouguang. Linqu was formerly called Changguo. In Kaihuang year six it was changed to Fengshan, and Banyang County was also established. At the beginning of Daye it was changed to Linqu, and Banyang was abolished into it. It had Feng Mountain, Yi Mountain, Muling Mountain, and Daxian Mountain. It had the Wen River and Wu River. Duchang had Ji Mountain, Fu Mountain, and Bailang Mountain. Beihai was formerly called Xiami, where Beihai Commandery was established. Later Qi changed the commandery to Gaoyang; at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Weizhou was divided off and established; at the beginning of Daye the province was abolished, and the county's name was changed. Yingqiu was abolished by Later Qi and restored in Kaihuang year sixteen. It had Congjiao Mountain and Nujie Mountain. Xiami was called Jiaodong by Later Wei and was abolished by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year six it was restored and changed to Weishui. At the beginning of Daye its name was changed. It had Tie Mountain and Gai River. Qi Commandery was formerly called Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 下密齊郡齊郡舊曰齊州。

translations.literal: Xiami. Qi Commandery: Qi Commandery was formerly called Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiami. Qi Commandery. Qi Commandery was formerly called Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣十，戶十五萬二千三百二十三。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 10 counties with a registered population of 152,323 households.

sentences.zh: 曆城舊置濟南郡，開皇初廢。大業初置齊郡，廢山茌縣入焉。有舜山、雞山、盧山、鵲山、華山、鮑山。祝阿臨邑臨濟開皇六年置，曰朝陽。十六年改曰臨濟，別置朝陽。大業初廢入焉。鄒平舊曰平原，開皇十八年改名焉。章丘舊曰高唐，開皇十六年改焉，又置營城縣。大業初廢入焉。又宋置東魏郡，後齊廢。有東陵山、長白山、龍盤山。長山舊曰武強，置廣川郡，並東清河、平原二郡入，改曰東平原郡。開皇初郡廢。又十六年置濟南縣，十八年改武強曰長山。大業初省濟南縣入焉。高苑後齊曰長樂。開皇十八年改為會城。大業初改焉。亭山舊曰衛國，後齊並土鼓，肥鄉入焉。開皇六年改名亭山。有龍舟山、儒山。淄川舊曰貝丘，置東清河郡。後齊郡廢。開皇十六年置淄州，十八年縣改名焉。大業初州廢。東萊郡舊置光州，開皇五年改曰萊州。

translations.literal: Licheng formerly had Jinan Commandery established, abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. At the beginning of Daye, Qi Commandery was established, and Shanchi County was abolished into it. It had Shun Mountain, Ji Mountain, Lu Mountain, Que Mountain, Hua Mountain, and Bao Mountain. Zhu'a, Linyi, and Linji: Linji was established in Kaihuang year six and called Chaoyang. In year sixteen it was changed to Linji, and Chaoyang was separately established. At the beginning of Daye, Chaoyang was abolished into it. Zouping was formerly called Pingyuan; in Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. Zhangqiu was formerly called Gaotang; in Kaihuang year sixteen it was changed, and Yingcheng County was also established. At the beginning of Daye Yingcheng was abolished into it. Song had also established Eastern Wei Commandery, which Later Qi abolished. It had Dongling Mountain, Changbai Mountain, and Longpan Mountain. Changshan was formerly called Wuqiang, where Guangchuan Commandery was established; Eastern Qinghe and Pingyuan commanderies were merged into it, and it was changed to Eastern Pingyuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Jinan County was also established, and in year eighteen Wuqiang was changed to Changshan. At the beginning of Daye Jinan County was abolished into it. Gaoyuan was called Changle by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Huicheng. At the beginning of Daye it was changed. Tingshan was formerly called Weiguo; Later Qi merged Tugu and Feixiang into it. In Kaihuang year six the name was changed to Tingshan. It had Longzhou Mountain and Ru Mountain. Zichuan was formerly called Beiqiu, where Eastern Qinghe Commandery was established. Later Qi abolished the commandery. In Kaihuang year sixteen Zizhou was established, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Donglai Commandery formerly had Guangzhou established, and in Kaihuang year five it was changed to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng formerly had Jinan Commandery established, abolished at the beginning of Kaihuang. At the beginning of Daye, Qi Commandery was established, and Shanchi County was abolished into it. It had Shun Mountain, Ji Mountain, Lu Mountain, Que Mountain, Hua Mountain, and Bao Mountain. Zhu'a, Linyi, and Linji: Linji was established in Kaihuang year six and called Chaoyang. In year sixteen it was changed to Linji, and Chaoyang was separately established. At the beginning of Daye, Chaoyang was abolished into it. Zouping was formerly called Pingyuan; in Kaihuang year eighteen its name was changed. Zhangqiu was formerly called Gaotang; in Kaihuang year sixteen it was changed, and Yingcheng County was also established. At the beginning of Daye Yingcheng was abolished into it. Song had also established Eastern Wei Commandery, which Later Qi abolished. It had Dongling Mountain, Changbai Mountain, and Longpan Mountain. Changshan was formerly called Wuqiang, where Guangchuan Commandery was established; Eastern Qinghe and Pingyuan commanderies were merged into it, and it was changed to Eastern Pingyuan Commandery. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen Jinan County was also established, and in year eighteen Wuqiang was changed to Changshan. At the beginning of Daye Jinan County was abolished into it. Gaoyuan was called Changle by Later Qi. In Kaihuang year eighteen it was changed to Huicheng. At the beginning of Daye it was changed. Tingshan was formerly called Weiguo; Later Qi merged Tugu and Feixiang into it. In Kaihuang year six the name was changed to Tingshan. It had Longzhou Mountain and Ru Mountain. Zichuan was formerly called Beiqiu, where Eastern Qinghe Commandery was established. Later Qi abolished the commandery. In Kaihuang year sixteen Zizhou was established, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Donglai Commandery formerly had Guangzhou established, and in Kaihuang year five it was changed to Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 淄川東萊郡東萊郡舊置光州，改曰萊州。

translations.literal: Zichuan. Donglai Commandery: Donglai Commandery formerly had Guangzhou established, changed to Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zichuan. Donglai Commandery, Donglai Commandery had formerly had Guangzhou established, changed to Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣九，戶九萬三百五十一。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 9 counties with a registered population of 90,351 households.

sentences.zh: 掖舊置東萊郡，後齊並曲城，當利二縣入焉。開皇初廢郡，大業初複置郡。有缶山。有掖水、光水。膠水舊曰長廣，仁壽元年改名焉。有明堂山。盧鄉後齊盧鄉及挺城並廢。開皇十六年複置盧鄉，並廢挺城入焉。即墨後齊及不其縣並廢。開皇十六年複，並廢不其入焉。有大勞山、馬山。有田橫島。觀陽後周廢。開皇十六年複，又分置牟州。大業初州廢。昌陽有巨神山。黃舊置東牟，長廣二郡，後齊廢東牟郡入長廣郡，開皇初郡廢。牟平有牟山、龍山、金山、九目山。文登後齊置。有石橋。有文登山、斥山、之罘山。高密郡舊置膠州，開皇五年改為密州。

translations.literal: Ye formerly had Donglai Commandery established; Later Qi merged Qucheng and Dangli counties into it. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and at the beginning of Daye it was restored. It had Fou Mountain. It had the Ye River and Guang River. Jiaoshui was formerly called Changguang; in Renshou year one its name was changed. It had Mingtang Mountain. Luxiang: Later Qi abolished both Luxiang and Tingcheng. In Kaihuang year sixteen Luxiang was restored, and Tingcheng was abolished into it. Jimo: Later Qi abolished both Jimo and Buqi County. In Kaihuang year sixteen Jimo was restored, and Buqi was abolished into it. It had Dalao Mountain and Ma Mountain. It had Tian Heng Island. Guanyang was abolished by Later Zhou. In Kaihuang year sixteen it was restored, and Mouzhou was also divided off and established. At the beginning of Daye the province was abolished. Changyang had Jushen Mountain. Huang formerly had Dongmou and Changguang commanderies established; Later Qi abolished Dongmou Commandery into Changguang Commandery, and at the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. Muping had Mou Mountain, Long Mountain, Jin Mountain, and Jiumu Mountain. Wendeng was established by Later Qi. It had Stone Bridge. It had Wendeng Mountain, Chi Mountain, and Zhifu Mountain. Gaomi Commandery formerly had Jiaozhou established, and in Kaihuang year five it was changed to Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 文登高密郡高密郡舊置膠州，開皇五年改為密州。

translations.literal: Wendeng. Gaomi Commandery: Gaomi Commandery formerly had Jiaozhou established; in the fifth year of Kaihuang it was changed to Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wendeng. Gaomi Commandery, Gaomi Commandery had formerly had Jiaozhou established; in the fifth year of Kaihuang it was changed to Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 統縣七，戶七萬一千九百二十。

translations.idiomatic: The commandery governed 7 counties with a registered population of 71,920 households.

sentences.zh: 諸城舊曰東武，置高密郡。開皇初郡廢，十八年縣改名焉。大業初複置郡。有烽火山。東莞後齊並姑幕縣入焉。有箕山、濰水。郚城舊置平昌郡。後齊廢郡，置琅邪縣，廢硃虛入焉。大業初改名郚城。安丘開皇十六年置，曰牟山。大業初改名，並省安昌入焉。高密後齊廢淳於縣入焉。膠西舊曰黔陬，置平昌郡。開皇初郡廢。十六年置縣，曰膠西。大業初又以黔陬入焉。琅邪開皇十六年置，曰豐泉。大業初改焉。有徐山、盧山、鄣日山、膠水。

translations.literal: Zhucheng was formerly called Dongwu, where Gaomi Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished, and in year eighteen the county's name was changed. At the beginning of Daye the commandery was restored. It had Fenghuo Mountain. Dongguan had Gumu County merged into it by Later Qi. It had Ji Mountain and the Wei River. Wucheng formerly had Pingchang Commandery established. Later Qi abolished the commandery, established Langye County, and abolished Zhuxu into it. At the beginning of Daye the name was changed to Wucheng. Anqiu was established in Kaihuang year sixteen and called Moushan. At the beginning of Daye its name was changed, and Anchang was also abolished into it. Gaomi had Chunyu County abolished into it by Later Qi. Jiaoxi was formerly called Qianzu, where Pingchang Commandery was established. At the beginning of Kaihuang the commandery was abolished. In year sixteen the county was established and called Jiaoxi. At the beginning of Daye Qianzu was again merged into it. Langye was established in Kaihuang year sixteen and called Fengquan. At the beginning of Daye it was changed. It had Xu Mountain, Lu Mountain, Zhangri Mountain, and Jiao River.

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, "Officers of the Regions": "Due east is called Qing Province."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, "Officers of the Regions": "Due east is called Qing Province."

sentences.zh: 其在天官，自須女八度至危十五度，為玄枵，於辰在子，齊之分野。

translations.literal: In the celestial offices, from eight degrees of Xu to fifteen degrees of Wei is the Dark Emptiness asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to zi; it is the allotted region of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the celestial offices, from eight degrees of Xu to fifteen degrees of Wei is the Dark Emptiness asterism; in the earthly branches it corresponds to zi; it is the allotted region of Qi, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 吳劄觀樂，聞齊之歌曰：「泱泱乎大風也哉，國未可量也。」

translations.literal: When Wu Zha observed music and heard the song of Qi, he said: "How vast and grand the wind! The state cannot be measured."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zha observed music and heard the song of Qi, he said: "How vast and grand the wind! The state cannot be measured."

sentences.zh: 在漢之時，俗彌侈泰，織作冰紈綺繡純麗之物，號為冠帶衣履天下。

translations.literal: In Han times the custom grew ever more extravagant; woven gauze, silk damask, fine embroidery, and pure brocade were called the crown and girdle, clothing and shoes for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the custom grew ever more extravagant; woven gauze, silk damask, fine embroidery, and pure brocade were called the crown and girdle, clothing and shoes for all under Heaven, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 始太公以尊賢尚智為教，故士庶傳習其風，莫不矜於功名，依於經術，闊達多智，志度舒緩。

translations.literal: At first Grand Duke Taigong made honoring the worthy and esteeming wisdom his teaching; hence gentry and commoners handed down the custom, all taking pride in merit and fame, relying on the classics, broad-minded and resourceful, with a relaxed and easy bearing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Grand Duke Taigong made honoring the worthy and esteeming wisdom his teaching; hence gentry and commoners handed down the custom, all taking pride in merit and fame, relying on the classics, broad-minded and resourceful, with a relaxed and easy bearing, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 其為失也，誇奢朋黨，言與行謬。

translations.literal: Their failing was boastfulness and cliquishness; words and deeds diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Their failing was boastfulness and cliquishness; words and deeds diverged, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 齊郡舊曰濟南，其俗好教飾子女淫哇之音，能使骨騰肉飛，傾詭人目。

translations.literal: Qi Commandery was formerly called Jinan; its custom loves teaching adornment to sons and daughters and decadent melodies that can make bones leap and flesh fly, overturning and bewitching men's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Commandery was formerly called Jinan; its custom loves teaching adornment to sons and daughters and decadent melodies that can make bones leap and flesh fly, overturning and bewitching men's eyes, as noted in the geography treatise.

translations.literal: The popular term "Qi singers" originally came from this.
translations.idiomatic: The popular term "Qi singers" originally came from this, as noted in the geography treatise.

sentences.zh: 祝阿縣俗，賓婚大會，肴饌雖豐，至於蒸膾，嘗之而已，多則謂之不敬，共相誚責，此其異也。

translations.literal: The custom of Zhu'e County: at guest feasts and wedding gatherings, though the dishes are abundant, they merely taste the steamed and minced meats; if there is too much, it is called disrespect, and they mock one another—this is their difference.
translations.idiomatic: The custom of Zhu'e County. At guest feasts and wedding gatherings, though the dishes are abundant, they merely taste the steamed and minced meats; if there is too much, it is called disrespect, and they mock one another—this is their difference.

sentences.zh: 大抵數郡風俗，與古不殊，男子多務農桑，崇尚學業，其歸於儉約，則頗變舊風。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the customs of these several commanderies differ little from antiquity; men mostly devote themselves to farming and sericulture and esteem learning; in returning to thrift and moderation, they have changed the old ways considerably.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole, the customs of these several commanderies differ little from antiquity; men mostly devote themselves to farming and sericulture and esteem learning; in returning to thrift and moderation, they have changed the old ways considerably.

sentences.zh: 東萊人尤朴魯，故特少文義。

translations.literal: The people of Donglai are especially plain and rustic, hence they are particularly lacking in literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Donglai are especially plain and rustic, hence they are particularly lacking in literary refinement, as noted in the geography treatise.
